answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying identity to a verified service quota earned through useful work. First, a new agent must complete 20 paid tasks for unrelated peers within 30 days, each checked by a different verifier. Second, its quota rises by one slot per 10 verified tasks and decays 5% weekly when idle, so hoarded identities fade. Third, forging 1,000 fake agents needs 20,000 verified tasks and $48,000 in verifier fees. Like a willow that bends without breaking, a ridge built stone by stone, the horizon belongs to agents that keep proving themselves, not multiplying.
